newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - ABARE sees 6.5 pct coarse grain output fall.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - ABARE sees 6.5 pct coarse grain output fall.

text.p: Australian coarse grain output is forecast to fall by 6.5 percent to 8.7 million tonnes in 1996/97 from 9.3 million tonnes last year, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday in its September quarter commodities report.
ABARE had estimated Australian production of 8.4 million tonnes in its June report.
The key barley crop, however, was forecast to rise by four percent to 5.7 million tonnes this year as a result of an increase in the area sown, ABARE said in its latest report.
"Excellent, if late, planting rains throughout south east Australia and Western Australia have led to generally good growing conditions for the Australian barley crop," it said.
"However, there are concerns over waterlogging and crop disease in some states, particularly Western Australia."
ABARE said the Australian barley price, a composite of feed and malting prices, was forecast to fall by 16.9 percent to A$182 per tonne, reflecting lower international prices.

"The strong recovery in world production is the main factor influencing barley prices this year, but stronger import demand for both feed and malting varieties will partly moderate the barley price falls expected in 1996/97," ABARE said.
